ModelValidatorExternal.release_notes:
### Project Switching

- **Switch Project No Longer Restarts the Application.** Choosing "Switch Project" previously closed and relaunched the whole app. It now reopens the Project Manager dialog in place and switches directly to the newly selected project, without an application restart.
- **Project Switch Is Blocked While a Simulation or Report Is Running.** Attempting to switch projects while a simulation or report generation is in progress now shows a message asking you to wait, instead of switching out from under an active run.
- **Fixed: A Previous Project's Case File Could Be Reused After Switching.** When switching projects without a restart, a case path left over from the previously open project could, in rare cases, still exist on disk and get silently reused for the new project. Case restoration now confirms the stored case actually lives inside the newly opened project's own folder before reusing it, and clears the selection otherwise so it falls back to discovery.

### Multi-Engine Validation Benchmarking

- **Validation Auto-Mapping Now Supports Any Number of Simulation Engines at Once.** Previously, automatic channel mapping only ever paired one PSSE handler against one PSCAD handler. Projects running multiple PSSE variants together (e.g. PSSE_UDM and PSSE_GENERIC) now get each handler mapped independently, with every handler that resolves the same channel automatically grouped into one benchmark comparison - so PSSE_UDM vs PSSE_GENERIC, or PSCAD vs both PSSE variants at once, all validate correctly without manual reconfiguration.
- **Fixed: Benchmark Plots Could Show the Wrong Handler's Channel Settings.** When two handlers shared the same channel name (common when comparing two PSSE variants), the plotting engine could pull the scaling/config info for the wrong one. Channel lookups are now disambiguated by handler, so each curve always uses its own settings.

### Validation Test Fixes

- **Fixed: Several Validation Tests Ignored Their Configured Time Tolerance.** Active Power Recovery, Reactive Power Rise Time, Voltage Rise Time, Reactive Current Response, Active Power Response, and the MISO balanced-fault-ride-through and VRT tests were reading a kwarg key that didn't match the configured field name, so the time-tolerance value from validation configuration was silently ignored (always `None`) even when set. These tests now correctly apply the configured time tolerance.

### PSSE Dynamics

- **New: Automatic Detection and Repair of Missing PLB Dynamics Models.** A PSSE test whose event requires a PLB-driven disturbance could previously run to completion and report success even though its selected DYR file had no active PLB model - silently producing a flat, event-less result. The app now checks for this at run time: if the selected DYR lacks an active PLB model, it automatically switches to a sibling DYR that has one, or - if none exists - generates one from an active GENCLS model in the case. Auto-generated files are clearly logged as not human-authored and should be reviewed before trusting compliance results that depend on them.

### Report Generation

- **Figure Captions and "Fig." Bookmarks Removed Under TocMode "None"/"Simple".** Every plot page previously printed a "Fig:X.Y TestID:..." caption and added a matching nested "Fig." bookmark, regardless of TocMode - redundant once each test already has its own unique TestID and a descriptive bookmark. These are now only generated under TocMode "Figures" or "Both", which actually build a List of Figures from them.
- **Report Header Line Breaks Are Now Preserved.** A multi-line Header (e.g. company name, project name, and study type typed on separate lines in the report config) was previously re-flowed into wrapped lines by width, discarding the line breaks you typed. Explicit line breaks are now preserved exactly as entered, in both PDF and Word reports.
- **Test Suite Name No Longer Printed on the First Plot Page Under TocMode "None".** Since the descriptive bookmarks already identify each test, the Test Suite Name heading is now omitted from the first page of each scenario when TocMode is "None".
- **Fixed: Plot Position Could Shift Between Pages Depending on Which Headings Were Shown.** The plot grid's position and size previously depended on whether the Title/Test Suite heading happened to be drawn on that particular page (e.g. suppressed under TocMode "None", or already shown earlier in a multi-page scenario). The space for these headings is now always reserved identically whether or not the text is actually drawn, so every plot sits at the same position and scale across all pages when scrolling through a report.

### Test Configuration Safety

- **Confirmation Dialog Before Resetting Config Files to Defaults.** Clicking the config refresh/reset button next to "Manage Configurations" previously overwrote any customised test configuration files immediately. It now shows a confirmation dialog explaining that customisations will be overwritten, before proceeding.

ModelValidator.release_notes:
### TSAT Channel Mapping & Validation

- **TSAT Channels Can Now Be Auto-Mapped and AI-Mapped.** The deterministic channel auto-mapper and the AI Validation Mapper previously only understood PSSE and PSCAD channels. Both now classify TSAT channels (POC/Grid/GEN) from the handler's Monitors selection and each channel's quantity/segment-type naming, and pair them into benchmark comparisons alongside PSSE and PSCAD the same way those two already were.

### MISO BPM-015 Test Additions and Corrections

- **New: Phase Angle Jump Ride-Through Test.** Validates that the model rides through each step of a phase-angle-jump event sequence without collapsing to near-zero.
- **New: Momentary Cessation Tests.** Two new tests check current-injection behavior during momentary cessation (current-blocking mode): one requires resuming injection within a configurable number of cycles after voltage recovery (Balanced FRT), the other requires the plant never enter momentary cessation at all (SVD/HVRT/LVRT).
- **New: Generic Flat-Run Test.** A body-agnostic flatness check with no fault/event to recover from, kept separate from MISO's own stricter initialization tests.
- **Changed: SCR Test No Longer Reports "Pass" for a Permissible Trip.** Tripping below the required SCR cutoff is allowed under BPM-015, but a plant that tripped did not have a fully satisfactory response - it now reports "Tripped" instead of "Pass" for that case.
- **Changed: MISO Trip Test No Longer Auto-Fails a Non-Trip.** Per BPM-015 Appendix G Sec. 5.1.9, a plant that doesn't trip for this disturbance isn't automatically non-compliant - it may reflect a permissible, intentionally wider ride-through design. This now reports "Unknown" (flagged for manual engineering review) instead of an automatic "Fail".
- **Fixed: SCR and Trip Tests Could Silently Stop Detecting a Trip.** The SCR test's pre-disturbance baseline was being measured against the wrong time window, and the general trip-detection threshold didn't account for a tripped unit settling on a small non-zero residual (station-service load, line charging current) rather than exact zero - both could cause a genuine trip to go undetected for the remainder of the run.
- **MISO SCR Test Now Checks Damping at Every Step.** The SCR profile steps through several levels with a fault at each transition; damping is now verified segment-by-segment across all of them instead of only once after the final event, so a poorly-damped response at an earlier step is no longer missed just because a later step recovers.
- **MISO PSCAD Initialization Test Now Actually Checks Settling Time.** The "reaches steady state within TimeSecsTolerance" half of this test was previously never evaluated - only post-initialization flatness was checked. It now measures real settling time from simulation start and fails if it exceeds the configured tolerance.

### High-Frequency Content Detection Rewrite

- **Fixed: HFC Test Could Miss Real Chattering Bursts.** The high-frequency-content check previously masked out the response immediately after each disturbance - the exact period it exists to examine - and compared against energy summed over the entire recording, diluting a short but severe burst into insignificance. It now evaluates each post-disturbance window on its own and reports the worst one.

### Validation Report Redesign

- **New: Per-Channel Plotly Validation Report.** The validation HTML report has been rebuilt around one interactive Plotly chart per channel, with collapsible test navigation, pass/fail badges, and a dashboard summary, replacing the previous static-image-based report.
- **Report Generation Now Runs Truly in Parallel.** Per-test config/result reads previously happened up front on the main thread before any subprocess started, serializing report generation despite spawning multiple worker processes. Each report subprocess now loads its own data independently, so reports generate concurrently as intended.
- **Report Generation Progress Now Shows Live Counts.** A status line (e.g. "Validation report: 3/12 done, 2 running") now accompanies the progress bar instead of a bare percentage.

### Reliability & Safety

- **New: Validation Workers Are Now Capped by Available Memory.** BackendValidator previously always started up to 20 concurrent validation workers regardless of system RAM, which could exhaust memory and crash with an obscure "Unable to allocate" error under real memory pressure. Worker count is now clamped to what currently available memory can plausibly support.
- **New: validation_configuration.toml Is Checked Before Any Test Runs.** A malformed or stale configuration (e.g. a duplicate section, or a test suite rule referencing a TestID that no longer exists) is now caught once, up front, with a clear message, instead of causing every spawned subprocess to independently fail the same way.
- **Fixed: A Broken Validation Config Could Silently Report Success.** When validation_configuration.toml failed to load, the suite's Validate button previously showed a false green "success" with no visible error anywhere in the UI. It now shows a clear failure state and status message explaining what went wrong.

### Project Switching

- **K-Factor and Compliance Computer Tool Dialogs Now Refresh on Project Switch.** An already-open K-Factor or Compliance Computer dialog previously kept showing the old project's test suites and channels after switching projects without a restart. Both now refresh automatically to the newly active project.

### PSSE Execution

- **PSSE Runs Now Route Through a Single Executable.** PSSE execution previously selected between separately-built executables per PSSE version (ModelValidatorPSSENew/3/4.exe). It now routes through one PSSE_ROUTER.exe that handles version selection internally.

### Other

- **"Unknown" Validation Results Now Shown Distinctly.** A result that needs manual engineering review (e.g. the MISO trip test's non-trip case) is now shown in amber in both the test tree and the per-test progress bar, instead of blending into the pass/fail coloring or ratio.
- **New: Regulatory Configuration Audit Tool.** A standalone tool (`general/regulatory_config_audit.py`) cross-references every regulatory body's real TestID list against validation_configuration.toml's coverage, flagging both untested TestIDs and stale rule references.
